source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's DFW1 campus in Carrollton, Texas publishes 45 MW of IT capacity across 600,000 square feet of technical space, making it the third-largest of the 19 Texas facilities that disclose a megawatt figure.

The number is the operator's own, not an estimate. It is also one of only 19 megawatt figures published across the 137 Texas data centers mapped here, and those 19 total 475.41 MW. The gap between 137 mapped and 19 publishing is the pattern that matters: most of the state's data center capacity cannot be counted from public disclosures at all, so any statewide total is a floor rather than a measure.

For AI specifically, the useful quantity is accelerators, and this data does not contain it. Converting 45 MW to racks requires a rack power assumption the operator does not publish. At 40 kW per rack, a common training density, 45 MW is roughly 1,125 racks. At 130 kW per rack, plausible for dense liquid cooling, it is about 346. The spec page states no rack count, no rack density, and no cooling method, so the accelerator count is not derivable here.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942, qualify the campus to host payment card data, protected health data, federal information systems, and audited financial controls, and TIA-942 speaks to the physical topology of the building. None of them name a customer, and the page publishes no address, postal code, or tenant list. What this data establishes is a power envelope and a compliance posture at one campus. It does not establish who runs inside it, how the power is converted into compute, or whether the 45 MW is fully subscribed.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
